slides.title: Raise prices in 2027, but only where customers can absorb them

paragraphs.text: PALISADE DOCS  |  2027 PRICING DECISION
Raise prices in 2027, but only where customers can absorb them
Should Palisade raise prices while customer churn is rising, and if so, how?
Discussion document for CEO Ravi Menon and the leadership team, December 2026
Based only on the 2027 pricing briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data). All figures are ARR in US$ unless stated.

slides.title: Executive summary: raise prices in 2027, but target mid-market and enterprise and keep SMB prices flat until a test proves they can rise

paragraphs.text: Executive summary: raise prices in 2027, but target mid-market and enterprise and keep SMB prices flat until a test proves they can rise

Answer: yes, with a targeted increase. At 2027 renewals, raise mid-market +12% and enterprise up to its contract terms. Hold SMB prices, exempt the 2025 promotion cohort and test core SMB before raising it. The plan adds ≈$4.1M of net ARR (the CFO's $10.3M headline is ≈$5.0M once timing and churn are counted), keeps NRR above 100%, and leaves the 15% growth target needing only ≈$0.9M of new-customer ARR.
Churn is rising because of one cohort, not because customers are reacting to price.

About 90% of the SMB churn rise (2.0% → 3.1% a month) comes from the 2,100 customers who joined on the 2025 half-price promotion. They churn at ≈4.9% a month. Churn among other SMB customers only moved from 2.0% to 2.1%, and the share of them citing price held at 18% (19% in 2025).
Pricing power sits in mid-market and enterprise, not SMB.

Mid-market and enterprise are 76% of ARR, with 112–118% NRR and monthly churn of 0.8% or less. A +10% mid-market test showed no significant conversion loss, and Inkwell has not appeared in deals above 200 seats. In SMB, Inkwell sells a $9 plan and Palisade's win rate against it fell from 51% to 38%.
The CFO's $10.3M is really ≈$5.0M. The targeted plan keeps ≈$4.1M of that with less risk.

Renewal timing and the 7% enterprise caps leave $7.6M that can be repriced in 2027, and expected churn cuts that to ≈$5.0M. Leaving SMB out costs ≈$1.0M in the base case. It raises the downside floor from $2.5M to $3.1M and avoids raising prices on customers who are already leaving over price.
Roll it out in stages, with guardrails.

Reprice mid-market and enterprise renewals from January, and drop mid-market to +10% if Q1 churn goes above 1.0% a month. Run a randomised +8% test on core SMB in Q1 and extend it from May only if it passes. Exempt the promotion cohort and fund its onboarding. Reset the budget line and define the churn figure the board sees.
Source: Palisade Docs 2027 pricing briefing pack (synthetic data); team analysis

slides.title: We tested the CFO's plan first. It held for mid-market and enterprise but failed on SMB and on value, so we changed the answer

paragraphs.text: We tested the CFO's plan first. It held for mid-market and enterprise but failed on SMB and on value, so we changed the answer
Initial hypothesis (CFO proposal): raise list prices 12% on every plan at renewal from January 2027, adding $10.3M of ARR.

data: What would have to be true
1. Rising churn is not a reaction to price across the customer base

About 90% of the SMB rise comes from the promotion cohort. Core SMB churn went 2.0% → 2.1% and its share citing price went 19% → 18%. But the promotion cohort itself left over price: 52% cite it, and most left within two months of the discount ending
Churn alone is no reason to freeze prices, but the promotion cohort must be exempt
2. Every segment can absorb +12% with little loss

Mid-market: a +10% test showed no significant conversion loss, 112% NRR, no Inkwell above 200 seats. Enterprise: 118% NRR, 0.2% churn. SMB: $9 Inkwell plan, win rate 51% → 38%, uplift roughly break-even in the downside case
Raise mid-market and enterprise; hold SMB and test it
Only $7.6M can be repriced in 2027: 15% of mid-market and 60% of enterprise ARR do not renew, and 7% caps apply. Expected churn takes it to ≈$5.0M
4. The plan keeps NRR above 100% and supports 15% growth
NRR rises from 109% to ≈114% (≈113% in the downside case). The 15% target then needs ≈$0.9M of new-customer ARR
The constraints don't stop it; the risk is in execution

paragraphs.text: Revised answer: raise prices where retention is strong (mid-market +12%, enterprise up to contract terms) and hold SMB, exempting the 2025 promotion cohort and testing core SMB before any increase.
Source: Palisade Docs 2027 pricing briefing pack (synthetic data); team analysis

slides.title: About 90% of the rise in SMB churn comes from the 2025 promotion cohort; churn among other SMB customers barely moved

paragraphs.text: 1  Why churn rose     2  Where pricing power is     3  What it is worth     4  How to execute
About 90% of the rise in SMB churn comes from the 2025 promotion cohort; churn among other SMB customers barely moved
SMB monthly logo churn, H1 2025 → H1 2026 (percentage points)
What this means
The promotion cohort is 36% of SMB customers and 21% of SMB ARR ($4.4M), but supplies ≈103 of the ≈183 SMB customers lost each month (56%).
Exit surveys tell the same story: the 34% overall price share implies the cohort makes up ≈47% of churners. That is close to the 56% estimated above.
The rise is a one-off effect from one cohort. As the cohort shrinks, blended SMB churn should drift back towards ≈2.1%.
Mid-market churn also edged up, from 0.6% to 0.8%. The pack gives no cause, so we treat it as a watch item (page 15).

Promotion cohort churn = (5,900 × 3.1% − 3,800 × 2.1%) ÷ 2,100 = 4.9% a month. Its effect = 2,100/5,900 × (4.9% − 2.1%) = 1.0pp, or 91% of the rise in churned customers. Uses mid-2026 customer counts for both halves.
Source: Palisade Docs 2027 pricing briefing pack (synthetic data); team analysis

slides.title: Promotion customers leave for two reasons, weak activation and the discount ending, so onboarding alone won't fix it and a price rise would hit them hardest

paragraphs.text: 1  Why churn rose     2  Where pricing power is     3  What it is worth     4  How to execute
Promotion customers leave for two reasons, weak activation and the discount ending, so onboarding alone won't fix it and a price rise would hit them hardest
Monthly churn, H1 2026: core SMB vs. 2025 promotion cohort (%)
Activation explains ≈30% of the cohort's extra churn
Only 41% of promotion customers sent 5+ documents in their first month, against 72% for other cohorts.
This supports the Head of Customer Success: many never set the product up.
The discount ending explains most of the rest (≈70%)
52% of promotion churners cite price, against 18% of core SMB churners.
Most promotion customers who left did so within two months of the 50% discount ending, so they reacted to a doubling of what they paid.
So what
The CFO is right that core churn is not about price, but wrong that churn is only an onboarding problem. This cohort has just shown it is very sensitive to price.
Exempt it from any 2027 increase ($4.4M ARR, 2,100 customers) and target onboarding at the 59% who never activated.

Activation effect: customers sending fewer than 5 documents in month 1 churn ≈3× as often. Core: 0.72c + 0.28×3c = 2.1% → c = 1.35%. Promotion cohort at 41% activated: 0.41c + 0.59×3c = 2.9%. The remaining 2.0pp is what activation doesn't explain.
Source: Palisade Docs 2027 pricing briefing pack (synthetic data); team analysis

slides.title: Only $7.6M of the CFO's $10.3M can be repriced in 2027, and expected churn cuts it to about $5.0M

paragraphs.text: 1  Why churn rose     2  Where pricing power is     3  What it is worth     4  How to execute
Only $7.6M of the CFO's $10.3M can be repriced in 2027, and expected churn cuts it to about $5.0M
CFO plan (+12% on every plan at renewal): 2027 ARR uplift, $M
How the numbers are built
Headline: 12% × $86.0M = $10.3M, as if all ARR renewed in 2027 with no caps.
Mid-market: 15% doesn't renew. 41.0 × 15% × 12% = 0.74.
Enterprise: 60% doesn't renew. 24.0 × 60% × 12% = 1.73.
Caps: 60% of the $9.6M renewing is assumed capped at 7%. 5.76 × 5pt = 0.29.
Churn give-back, by segment: SMB 1.54 (core 1.00 + promotion 0.53), mid-market 0.94, enterprise 0.05.
All figures are exit-2027 ARR run-rate. In-year revenue will be lower because renewals are spread across the year.
If the $10.3M is in the 2027 budget, the plan has a hole of ≈$5.3M before any downside.
Renewal timing and contract terms: −$2.8M
Churn from the price rise (page 9): −$2.5M

paragraphs.text: Net uplift formula, per segment
Net = repriced ARR × p − repriced ARR × (1 + p) × loss rate
28% and 6% are the 2023 relative jumps: 2.3/1.8 − 1 during the six-month spike, and 1.9/1.8 − 1 afterwards.
Limits of these assumptions
Loss is assumed to scale linearly with the size of the increase. +12% is beyond the tested +8% (SMB) and +10% (mid-market).
Effects on new-customer win rates are not counted. That understates the cost of an SMB increase while Inkwell is pressing.
The downside case doubles every rate to cover Inkwell and renewal customers reacting more strongly than new sign-ups.

slides.title: With the targeted plan, 2027 ARR reaches ≈$98.0M before new customers, so 15% growth needs only ≈$0.9M of new-customer ARR

paragraphs.text: 1  Why churn rose     2  Where pricing power is     3  What it is worth     4  How to execute
With the targeted plan, 2027 ARR reaches ≈$98.0M before new customers, so 15% growth needs only ≈$0.9M of new-customer ARR
ARR bridge, 2026 → 2027 target, $M
The NRR constraint holds in every case
Overall NRR: 109% today, ≈114% with the plan, ≈113% in the downside case. The CFO plan's downside is ≈112%.
SMB NRR stays below 100% (94%) under every option. That is a cohort problem, and price won't fix it.
Growth target: reachable, but it depends on new customers
$0.9M is ≈28 mid-market customers at the $30k average, or ≈200 core SMB customers at $4.4k.
Downside: $1.8M needed. The SMB option (+$0.5M) and +12% holding in mid-market are the buffers.
Each 1pt of NRR is worth $0.86M. The pack has no history of new-customer ARR, so this is the key planning assumption to check.
Existing base: 21.0 × 94% + 41.0 × 112% + 24.0 × 118% = 94.0, so NRR is 109.3%. Assumes trailing NRR repeats in 2027 and contains no price increase.
Source: Palisade Docs 2027 pricing briefing pack (synthetic data); team analysis

slides.title: A three-month randomised test will show whether core SMB customers can bear +8% before Palisade commits to it

paragraphs.text: 1  Why churn rose     2  Where pricing power is     3  What it is worth     4  How to execute
A three-month randomised test will show whether core SMB customers can bear +8% before Palisade commits to it
Test design
Who: core SMB customers renewing in Q1 2027. The promotion cohort is excluded.
Split: 50/50 at random by account. Treatment +8% at renewal with standard notice; control at today's price.
Main metric: monthly logo churn in the 90 days after renewal, treatment minus control.
Secondary metrics: downgrades to cheaper plans, share of exit surveys citing price, Inkwell mentions.

Statistical power: with ≈1,900 customers per arm and ≈6.3% three-month churn in the control group, the standard error of the difference is ≈0.8pp. That separates a 2023-type reaction (+1.5pp over 3 months) from break-even (+3.7pp) by ≈2.6 standard errors.
Caveat: annual-plan customers renew only once a year. If they are a large share of SMB, fewer accounts will renew in Q1, so extend the test to six months.
Decision rule: extra monthly churn, treatment vs control (pp)
Roll out from May
Hold and extend test
Stop
+0.5pp a month
Break-even:
+1.2pp a month
Where the thresholds come from
+8% pays back if less than 0.08 ÷ 1.08 = 7.4% of repriced ARR is lost within 12 months. Spread over a six-month spike, as in 2023, that is ≈1.2pp a month.
In 2023, SMB churn rose 0.5pp a month for six months, well under break-even. Rolling out only below 0.6pp keeps a margin for Inkwell and for longer-lasting effects.
Value if it passes: +8% on ≈2/3 of core SMB ARR repriced May–Dec = $0.9M gross, ≈$0.5M net.
Source: Palisade Docs 2027 pricing briefing pack (synthetic data); team analysis

slides.title: Onboarding is worth funding, but it won't halve SMB churn in two quarters; plan on a 15–20% cut for new customers

paragraphs.text: 1  Why churn rose     2  Where pricing power is     3  What it is worth     4  How to execute
Onboarding is worth funding, but it won't halve SMB churn in two quarters; plan on a 15–20% cut for new customers
SMB monthly logo churn: today and with onboarding (%)
Why the 'halve churn' claim doesn't hold
Halving means 3.1% → 1.55%. Even if every SMB customer behaved like an activated one, churn would be ≈1.35%, so halving would need almost every customer activated.
First-month activation can't be applied retroactively to the 5,900 existing customers. Onboarding mainly affects new sign-ups.
A realistic aim is to raise new-customer activation from 72% to 85%. That cuts new-cohort churn from 2.1% to ≈1.75% (−17%).
Blended SMB churn will fall anyway as the promotion cohort shrinks. Measure onboarding by cohort, or its effect will look bigger than it is.
Implication
Fund onboarding for new customers and outreach to the promotion cohort as the churn levers. Keep them out of the 2027 ARR plan until cohort data shows the effect.
Activated churn c from 0.72c + 0.28 × 3c = 2.1% → c = 1.35%. Non-activated 3c = 4.0%. At 85% activation: 0.85c + 0.15 × 3c = 1.75%.
Source: Palisade Docs 2027 pricing briefing pack (synthetic data); team analysis

slides.title: Appendix: the board dashboard's '1.4% → 2.3%' cannot be rebuilt from segment data and should be replaced with defined measures

paragraphs.text: Appendix: the board dashboard's '1.4% → 2.3%' cannot be rebuilt from segment data and should be replaced with defined measures

data: Core SMB logo churn (excluding the promotion cohort)

paragraphs.text: Why it matters and what to report instead
Leadership is discussing 'rising churn' using a number no one can trace. Depending on the weighting, the same data gives a +0.4pp or a +0.9pp rise.
Recommended board set: (1) monthly logo churn by segment; (2) SMB churn split into core and promotion cohort; (3) gross ARR churn; (4) NRR by segment, each with a written definition.
Those measures also show the guardrails in this plan: the mid-market renewal trigger and the SMB test arms.
Source: briefing pack Table 1 and section 10; team analysis. Weights use mid-2026 customer counts and ARR for both periods.
